problem: Protect the public and the brand after product tampering.
title: Johnson & Johnson recalls Tylenol and launches tamper-resistant packaging
context: Seven people died after taking Tylenol capsules laced with cyanide in the Chicago area in 1982.
decision_made: Recall about 31 million bottles and relaunch with tamper-resistant packaging.
action_taken: Unveiled triple-sealed packaging on 11 November 1982, 43 days after the first deaths.
observed_outcome: Tylenol's market share fell from about 37 percent to about 7 percent during the crisis and was back to about 30 percent within a year. The packaging became an industry standard.
lessons: Acting quickly and visibly on safety, even at large cost, can preserve trust in a brand.
limitations: Recall cost and share figures vary by source (about $100 million most often cited). Other factors, such as coupons, contributed to the recovery. One unsourced claim of a 70 percent recovery in five months was excluded.

claims.claim_text: J&J recalled about 31 million Tylenol bottles and relaunched with tamper-resistant packaging.
Tylenol's market share fell to about 7 percent and recovered to about 30 percent within a year.
